name: Verra

summary.text: Verra is a Washington-based nonprofit that runs the Verified Carbon Standard, the largest registry for voluntary carbon credits. In January 2023 The Guardian, Die Zeit and SourceMaterial published an analysis of Verra-approved rainforest (REDD+) projects concluding that most credits did not represent real emissions reductions; Verra publicly rejected the methodology. Its chief executive David Antonioli announced in May 2023 that he would leave in June, giving no reason. Verra later suspended projects of C-Quest Capital after that developer disclosed over-issued cookstove credits.

facts.claim: In January 2023 a nine-month investigation by The Guardian, Die Zeit and SourceMaterial reported that more than 90% of Verra's rainforest offsets examined were likely worthless; it found that only eight of 29 Verra-approved projects where analysis was possible showed evidence of reduced deforestation.
facts.quote: it found that just eight out of 29 Verra-approved projects where analysis was possible showed evidence of reduced deforestation

sources.title: Verra disputes Guardian findings on 'worthless' REDD credits
Verra boss steps down after criticism of its carbon credits

facts.claim: Verra rejected the findings, arguing that the synthetic-control studies the reporting relied on do not consider site-specific drivers of deforestation, and citing a 2022 University of Cambridge study of 40 REDD+ projects.
facts.quote: they have limited utility for assessing the impact of REDD projects because they do not consider site-specific drivers of deforestation

facts.claim: Verra said it had its most senior experts conduct a technical review of the article and the three studies behind it.

facts.claim: Verra CEO David Antonioli announced on May 23, 2023 that he would leave on June 16; he gave no reason, and president Judith Simon became interim CEO.
facts.quote: He was set to leave the Washington-based Verra on June 16, according to a May 23 post on his LinkedIn page.

openQuestions: Site claim (reported; Verra disputed, CEO stepped down months later): supported. No source states the resignation was caused by the investigation; Climate Home News reported no reason was given.
Verra's own statement on Antonioli's departure (verra.org/verra-ceo-to-step-down/) is cited by the site but was not opened here.
